What should ticket 08 ship for an expects_from edge that closes a cycle, and what follow-up work (if any) goes into separate tickets?
records.selected_option_title: Parent link yields, other cycles fail naming the edges, plus a data-fix ticket

records.title: Native read-only GitHub source for facts that feed decisions, with host handoff only for ...
records.question: Decide how the Leafcutter decision kernel should get read access to GitHub (pull requests, CI check results and run times, issues) so it can answer questions such as whether CI is green or whether open pull requests should be combined. Options: a native read-only retrieval source inside the kernel that pulls from the GitHub API into evidence; a host tool, where the kernel hands GitHub lookups to the host LLM (Claude Code or Codex) which runs gh; or another option grounded in the repository.
records.selected_option_title: Native read-only GitHub source for facts that feed decisions, with host handoff only for anything beyond reading

records.title: one decision-lifecycle flow whose steps expand to four sub-flows
records.question: Decide how to model the Leafcutter decision lifecycle in the product-truth store (docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/) so it shows end to end how a decision is formed, staged as a record, published into docs/decisions, and retrieved as precedent by a later run. Options: four separate flows, one per stage; one decision-lifecycle flow whose steps expand to four sub-flows; or another option grounded in the repository.
records.selected_option_title: one decision-lifecycle flow whose steps expand to four sub-flows

records.title: Render the Codex skill from the same in-package source into the workspace root where ...
records.question: Decide how to make the Leafcutter kernel procedure (the /leafcutter skill for Claude Code) usable from OpenAI Codex, both the CLI and the IDE extension. Codex 0.160 has no custom slash commands any more; it runs skills from .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (repo) or ~/.agents/skills (user), invoked explicitly as $leafcutter, with agents/openai.yaml able to forbid implicit invocation; it ignores allowed-tools, blocks network in its default sandbox unless config.toml enables network_access or a .codex/rules prefix_rule allows a command, and offers structured questions only in Plan mode, so kernel questions are asked as plain text. Options: a repo-level skill in .agents/skills/leafcutter with a .codex/rules prefix rule that allows only the kernel command; a user-level skill in ~/.agents/skills/leafcutter with network access enabled in ~/.codex/config.toml; or another option grounded in the repository.
records.selected_option_title: Render the Codex skill from the same in-package source into the workspace root where sessions run, with the repository root fixed at install time and a prefix rule for the kernel command

records.title: Category records (SKOS-style labels) that hold membership as (decision id, criterion id) ...
records.question: Decide the storage format for reusable decision criteria (the decision basis the kernel reuses across decisions). Today each run's criteria are generated per decision and stored only inside docs/decisions/dec-*.yaml records. Options: a) one YAML file per criterion in a new docs/criteria/ folder (same style as the decision records, ADR-059 'YAML now, graph later'); b) one catalog YAML of criterion categories, each listing its member criteria; c) keep criteria inside decision records and generate a criteria index from them; d) another option grounded in the repository. The format must be Git-reviewable, projectable into Neo4j, and carry what clustering and reuse need (category, decision_type, components, usage and outcome counts).
records.selected_option_title: Category records (SKOS-style labels) that hold membership as (decision id, criterion id) references

records.title: Step 0 prerequisites, then DK-400 in 3 and DK-500 in 4 dependency-checked epics, one at a ...
records.question: How should we build the two approved Decision Kernel AC trees with /build-ac and then /build-feature: DK-500 reusable decision criteria (57 leaf ACs) and DK-400 split compound requests (50 leaf ACs)? Decide the build order, the epic size (one epic per tree or one epic per L1), whether the trees run in parallel, and what must happen before the first build starts.
records.selected_option_title: Step 0 prerequisites, then DK-400 in 3 and DK-500 in 4 dependency-checked epics, one at a time

records.title: Jev judging 'same question?' for candidate pairs against existing categories
records.question: Decide how the Leafcutter decision kernel should group reusable decision criteria into categories (AC DK-300b): criteria that ask the same thing in different words must end up in one category with one preferred wording, related categories may sit under a broader one, and every grouping stays a suggestion a person can accept, change or undo. The storage format is already decided (dec-93c1c730463c1f3c: category records with SKOS-style labels that hold (decision id, criterion id) membership), and candidates come from published decision records and Langfuse run history. Options: a) deterministic wording or label matching (content-word overlap, as precedent lookup uses today); b) embedding-similarity clustering of criterion questions; c) Jev judging 'same question?' for candidate pairs against existing categories; d) an LLM proposes the groupings for human approval; e) a staged mix ordered by ADR-053 (deterministic first, then Jev, then an LLM, then the human); or another option grounded in the repository.
records.selected_option_title: Jev judging 'same question?' for candidate pairs against existing categories

records.title: Publish directly when the important gates are met and the decision is not risky, through ...
records.question: Decide when the Leafcutter decision kernel may publish an approved decision record into docs/decisions by itself and when it must ask the user first, recorded as a policy decision file. Today publishing is an explicit human-run command (ADR-060) and every record is human-approved. Options: always ask the user before publishing; publish directly unless the decision supersedes or corrects an existing record or changes an accepted ADR or policy, and ask otherwise; or another option grounded in the repository.
records.selected_option_title: Publish directly when the important gates are met and the decision is not risky, through a new PR flow copied from finalize-feature

records.title: Make the kernel the default entry for design, planning and lookup questions in Claude ...
records.question: Decide what to build next for the Leafcutter decision kernel so that it is wired into the real development workflow and has direct impact. Today nothing outside kernel/ and the /leafcutter skill calls the kernel, and docs/decisions holds one record, while design decisions answered by the user in Claude Code sessions are not recorded anywhere the kernel can reuse. Options: run trace analyzers over the recent kernel traces; file human decisions made in Claude Code sessions as decision records; have agents consult the kernel for precedent before asking the user a design question, applying standing policies such as POL-GIT-001 directly; or another option grounded in the repository.
records.selected_option_title: Make the kernel the default entry for design, planning and lookup questions in Claude Code sessions

records.title: Kernel-contract YAML per decision
records.question: Decide how Leafcutter should file decision records as JSON or YAML files under docs/ so later kernel runs can find and reuse them as precedent: which fields a record needs, which classification filters it carries (component, file type or language, repository-wide, roadmap phase), the folder layout and file naming, and how human approval and later corrections are recorded.
